status: Partial software implementation; surface/swapchain and window compositor integration remain open.

implementation: Private NVKMD canonical-BO import takes an independent mutable reference before describing backing. Outputs publish only after normal VA/binding/residency succeeds; the ordinary NVK device memory list and SHARED flag retain standard lookup/unref semantics.

Actual RAM/VRAM placement, transfer/CPU access, exact adapter/memory generation and complete aligned extent are validated. Geometry/modifier is preserved without claiming image-layout compatibility. Import cleanup only drops newly owned resources; stale source handles do not poison a healthy recipient device.
checks: Canonical R4VK build (512 C units plus identity), C/Zig ABI conformance and R4M container/relocation validation.
Private consumer compiles the actual NVKMD/device/memory/VA/submit/sync owners against current pinned Mesa inputs; SMP4 real kernel BO/import/broker integration.

Four image-backing cases: mappable RAM, GPU-only RAM, modeled linear VRAM, modeled modifier VRAM. Two logical devices import one BO; producer and sibling import close while remaining import retains identical descriptor/backing. NVK VA lookup and ordinary unref are used.

Thirteen targeted faults: reference capacity, immutable, mapping-only, wrong adapter, wrong memory generation, truncated extent, missing transfer usage, zero alignment, VA OOM, binding OOM, and host allocations at metadata/VA/binding. Every recoverable error preserves outputs and source, returns resources to the live-source baseline, then permits retry.
Stale/zero source, too-short extent, absent import capability and lost backend property receipt reject. Device-lost persists after properties return; source ref remains independently releasable.

Pending modeled native job retains real residency after source and NVK memory free; completion, fence and context cleanup return all BO/reference/lease/backing/pinning/mapping counters to baseline. C port active allocations return to zero.
limitations: This exercises private memory-owner integration, not public Vulkan WSI, VkImage creation, presentation, pixels or physical GPU execution. The canonical library is built separately; no public import extension is added.

Driver and some returned metadata/errors are modeled. The opaque modifier only checks preservation, not an actual NVIDIA/NIL layout match. Imported access flags are fault-injected; underlying kernel sharing remains real.
Both logical devices belong to the probe process. Cross-process window/service ownership and app-crash/desktop-restart admission remain work for this subversion.

Compiler/logging failure sinks in the private fixture trap if called; they neither simulate successful compiler work nor complete GPU operations. The full canonical library retains its actual compiler/runtime.
No new permanent test group and no physical OssiPC access. Hardware recipe remains OssiGPU.txt /0.79.37.

remaining: Common GPU window-buffer transport/consumer lifetime with exact program/window/desktop generations.
Native surface discovery and actual KHR swapchain/acquire/present with shared capability/color/capture/output policy.
Targeted resize/hide/hotplug/app-abort/desktop-restart software integration and later physical recipe.

implementation: Private WSI image constructor imports the canonical BO through existing NVKMD memory/VA owners, validates exact channel format, dimensions, planes, stride, modifier and actual NVK/NIL format capabilities before binding.

Original NVK creates the image and kind-aware VA. An ordinary Vulkan memory wrapper owns the imported backing, follows heap accounting and normal DestroyImage/FreeMemory. No second GPU backing or pixel initialization is introduced by import.

Native uncompressed tiled allocation now uses the same backing allocator with kind-aware VA, enabling original NVK tiled shadows for linear images mixed with depth/tiled attachments. GOB dimensions remain in NIL/commands; compression and foreign BO flags are not invented.
Cleanup destroys the image before imported memory; failures preserve outputs and the producer reference. Public FD/DRM/WSI extensions remain unadvertised.
checks: Canonical R4VK build (513 C units plus identity), C/Zig ABI conformance and R4M container/relocation validation.

One scoped SMP4 private consumer links the full current production NVK/NIL/NAK archives without compiler/libc substitutes. The driver calls the actual NVIDIA surface layout calculator; kernel BO/native/VA brokers are real.

Eight 127x65 images: 8-bit UNORM, sRGB, 10-bit and FP16, each linear and blocklinear. Exact descriptor, channel order, row stride, NIL size, modifier/PTE kind, same BO with independent reference, and image/memory ownership are checked.

Producer closes before image-view/render use. Actual Vulkan dynamic-rendering clear, barriers, queue submission and fence wait run with modeled completion. The linear UNORM case includes a depth attachment and requires NVK to allocate its normal tiled shadow.

Wrong channel format, depth/undefined format, zero/unsupported usage and stale source reject. Callback OOM at image and memory wrapper preserves output, balances callbacks, restores the live-source BO baseline and permits retry. Repeated finish is harmless.
Each image cleanup balances Vulkan heap usage; final device/instance teardown restores exact pre-instance BO/reference/lease/backing/pinning/mapping counters and zero active C allocations.
limitations: Private image foundation only: no public native surface, KHR swapchain, cross-process GPU window transport or compositor integration yet.

NVIDIA capability receipts, GPU allocation/addresses and completion are modeled. Actual layout calculation, NIL layout and Vulkan command production run; GPU instructions, pixel values, physical display and performance are not verified.
The canonical R4L is built separately. The private image helper is consumed by a fixture linked to the same production archives and is not yet reachable through a public R4VK API.
No additional permanent test group or OssiPC contact. Physical pixels, mixed linear/depth shadow copy and presentation remain in OssiGPU.txt /0.79.37.
